text:
sarah: Heads up — saw a weird thing in the latency dashboard: p95 is showing lower than p50 for the /v1/generate endpoint after we flipped the debounce routing policy. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.internal/shot.png :eyes:
leo: Huh. Can you paste the dashboard query or time window?
sarah: 30m window, p50/p95 lines by endpoint. Here's the console query I used:
```
SELECT endpoint, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.5) AS p50, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) AS p95
FROM latency_events
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND time >= now() - interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY endpoint
```
amanda: Two quick suspects: 1) sampling / downsampling across shards + t-digest interpolation can make top quantiles non-monotonic if counts are tiny per-shard, 2) retry/cached short-circuit responses changing sample mix.
sanjay: Also the debounce routing we added fans requests to a fast-cache path for some clients; that injects a bunch of low-latency events that only show up on the endpoint breakdown but not on the global rollup because of sampling differences. That can pull p50 up or p95 down depending on weights.
leo: Is the dashboard using raw samples or the rolled-up tdigest? If it's t-digest rollups, merging order and compression can invert percentiles in edge cases.
sarah: Dashboard uses rollups (tdigest) for the historical pane and raw stream for live. The discordance appears only after the rollout of debounce routing 14:12 UTC.
amanda: Quick repro steps: 1) compare sample counts per endpoint (if p95<p50 you'll likely see low sample_count on the endpoint slice). 2) run a raw-scan of the same window without tdigest and compute exact percentiles. 3) check for lots of identical tiny latencies (cache hits / gateway fast-path) that would change distribution tail.
sanjay: I ran a raw scan for the same 30m window. Endpoint A: sample_count=87, p50=240ms, p95=180ms. Endpoint B: sample_count=1200, p50=260ms, p95=420ms. Combined rollup (weighted) ended up showing p95 lower because tdigest merge produced a skewed tail when Endpoint A's small t-digest dominated certain centroids.
sarah: OK that matches what I'm seeing. What's the recommended fix short-term?
amanda: Short-term: add a sample_count overlay on the latency series and fade/annotate slices with sample_count < 200. Also for the rollout, exclude fast-cache path from percentile rollups until we have consistent sampling. Medium-term: switch to hybrid storage where small-sample exact percentiles are recomputed from raw events rather than merged t-digests.
leo: Agree. UX-wise we should surface a badge on every percentile line: "sample_count=N (raw/rollup)" and an explanation hover that non-monotonic quantiles can happen with merged sketches. Saves support tickets.
sanjay: I'll add an annotations PR to the console: when endpoint slice sample_count < 250 show a warning and link to the runbook.
opsbot: deploy-bot: changelist CL-4521 created by sanjay for console annotation. CI queued. :rocket:
sarah: Thanks everyone — filing an incident note and adding the annotation to the dashboard changelog. Will revert debounce routing for a small subset if we see customer impact. :thumbsup:
